findings.title: Leyte-Cebu reached a binding limit on 116 of 119 days
findings.stat: A row literally named LEYTE_TO_CEBU appears in the day-ahead runs on 95 of 119 days
findings.blurb: IEMOP's congestion files name equipment that reached its limit. The Tabango (Leyte) to Daanbantayan (Cebu) 230 kV lines had the most days at a limit, 116 of 119 archive days across the day-ahead and real-time runs, including 139 5-minute real-time intervals on 27 days. IEMOP's December 2025 report names the same transmission path.
findings.source: IEMOP congestions-manifesting files (RTD + DAP), archive window

findings.title: Announced data-center demand is a large share of the supply margin
findings.stat: 1,500 MW forecast (DICT, by 2028) against a 3,629 MW May 2026 system supply margin
findings.blurb: The DICT forecast alone equals 41% of the whole system's May margin; Meralco has committed 1,000 MW for 10 data centers. The 11 pinned sites with a public figure name 591.3 MW between them, and a data center is near-flat 24/7 load: it consumes margin in every interval, not just at the evening peak.
findings.source: IEMOP May 2026 report; DICT via BusinessWorld; PCIJ

findings.title: Reserves ran below requirement on most days
findings.stat: Luzon scheduled reserves fell below the stated requirement on 73 of 119 archive days
findings.blurb: In the operator's own dispatch schedules, load was curtailed on 106 grid-days in this window (5,222.4 MWh), and the Visayas ran short of scheduled reserves on 72 days. Thin margins are the observed normal state, not a forecast.
findings.source: IEMOP RTD regional summaries, archive window

findings.title: Regional prices separated after market trading resumed
findings.stat: Administered window: the three grids priced within P0.015/kWh of each other. Market window: a mean daily high-to-low spread of P5.29/kWh across the three grids
findings.blurb: While WESM was suspended (through 2026-05-01), daily regional prices were near-identical. After trading resumed, the islands split: Luzon P7.53, Visayas P12.38, Mindanao P11.13 per kWh on average, with 38 days spreading beyond P5/kWh and a widest daily spread of P15.722/kWh on 2026-06-08. Limited transfer capacity lets regional prices separate when local supply and demand differ.
findings.source: IEMOP load-weighted average prices (final), archive window

findings.title: One plant trip takes 18% of the margin with it
findings.stat: One 647 MW Sual unit equals 18% of the May 2026 system margin
findings.blurb: Sual's two 647 MW units are among the largest on the Luzon grid, though not the largest: GNPower Dinginin runs 2x668 MW, and the market's own Luzon contingency reserve requirement sits at that same 668 MW. The archive's outage schedules list a Sual unit out on 0 days in this window; the map's toggle subtracts one unit from the published margin as arithmetic, not a dispatch simulation.
findings.source: IEMOP outage schedules used in RTD; IEMOP May 2026 report

findings.title: A 52-day Visayas alert streak just ended
findings.blurb: The streak ended when one 150 MW unit returned; 935.3 MW was still unavailable that day. In the same window the dispatch schedules show the Visayas short of scheduled reserves on 72 days, with 514.61 MWh of load curtailed in the schedules on 2026-06-25 alone.
findings.source: NGCP advisories via SunStar and GMA (Jul 1-2, 2026); IEMOP RTD regional summaries
